title: Develop a "Zedu vs. Slack/Discord" Comparison Guide
description: Create a comprehensive comparison explaining why general chat tools fall short for structured learning environments. The goal is to highlight Zedu’s specific features—cohort-specific channels, AI summarization, and educator roles—to show how Zedu reduces admin overhead

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Build the comparison as a dated feature matrix with a 'not published' column instead of guesses
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Structure the guide around a feature-by-feature matrix (channels, threads, file storage, roles, notifications, pricing) with three columns: Zedu, Slack, Discord. Every cell cites the source it came from (official pricing or help page) with an access date, and anything not verifiable from public pages goes into an explicit 'not published' column rather than an estimate. End with an honest 'where Zedu is weaker' section - that honesty is what makes a comparison page survive editor and reader scrutiny.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Build the comparison from same-week live checks, with honest "where they win" rows
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A Zedu vs Slack/Discord guide that survives scrutiny: every row built from live checks done the same week (channels and threads, live classes, attendance records, file handoffs, permissions, pricing — each cell citing the zedu.chat page or app screen it came from, and the competitor's public pricing/docs page). Include rows where Slack or Discord genuinely win today (integrations marketplace, public-community features) — the honesty is the differentiator, matching the tone of the approved "what Zedu does not do" direction. Deliverable: one /resources article plus the row-by-row evidence table so any agent can re-verify before publishing. No invented numbers anywhere.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Compare Zedu against Slack and Discord for cohort learning, feature by feature
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A single comparison page that tests Zedu against Slack and Discord on what matters for structured learning: cohort-specific channels with educator roles, AI summarization of class threads, file and assignment persistence, Buzz live-class integration, and admin oversight. Each section states what Slack/Discord do well, where they break for paid cohorts, and when Zedu is the right move versus when a group chat is fine. All claims sourced from public pages. Deliverable: one page with title under 60 chars, meta under 160, a feature table, an FAQ from real buyer questions, and internal links from pricing and blog.
